nodes.description: Missense alleles at buried residues of the CORE domain, away from the nucleotide sites, that are expected to act by destabilizing the fold and lowering the amount of enzyme in the red cell. Tyr164 is fully buried (relative side-chain accessibility 0.01 in PDB 1Z83, 11.8 A from Ap5A) and packs against Phe12, Leu115, Val160 and Ile161; it is invariant from Escherichia coli adenylate kinase to human AK1. Recombinant Tyr164Cys is grossly unstable, and the homozygous patient had no detectable erythrocyte enzyme protein on electrophoresis. The c.518T>G allele, which changes the buried strand residue Val173 to glycine on the canonical transcript, is placed in this class on structural grounds only. A mature red cell cannot replace an unstable protein, so instability becomes absence of activity as the cell ages.

evidence.reference_title: Erythrocyte adenylate kinase deficiency: characterization of recombinant mutant forms and relationship with nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
evidence.snippet: Four mutant enzymes (Gly40Arg, Gly64Arg, Arg128Trp, Asp140del) were severely affected in activity, displaying a catalytic efficiency of four orders of magnitude lower than the wild-type; one (Tyr164Cys) was grossly perturbed in protein stability.

nodes.description: Missense and single-residue deletion alleles that alter residues lining the AMP and ATP sites of AK1. AK1 is a 194-residue monomer with a central CORE domain, an NMP-binding domain (residues 38-67) and a LID domain (residues 131-141) that close over the two nucleotides during phosphoryl transfer. In the crystal structure of human AK1 with the bisubstrate analog Ap5A (PDB 1Z83, chain A; distances computed for this entry), Gly40 (3.5 A), Gly64 (4.4 A), Arg97 (3.5 A), Gln101 (3.1 A), Arg128 (3.4 A), Arg138 (3.2 A) and Asp140 (4.0 A) all lie within 4.5 A of the ligand, and Gln24 sits 5.2 A away on the helix that follows the phosphate-binding loop. The recombinant Gly40Arg, Gly64Arg, Arg128Trp and Asp140del enzymes retain about one ten-thousandth of wild-type catalytic efficiency, and Arg97Trp loses about 89% of catalytic efficiency with weakened binding of all three nucleotides. These are loss-of-function alleles; affected individuals are homozygous or compound heterozygous and carriers are healthy, so there is no evidence of a dominant-negative or gain-of-function effect.

nodes.description: Nonsense and frameshift alleles that remove or replace the C-terminal part of the enzyme. Arg107Ter and the frameshifts Val47SerfsTer45 (reported as delG138) and Met75AsnfsTer19 stop translation before the LID domain and before the nucleotide-site residues Arg128, Arg132 and Gly177, so any product lacks a complete active site; these transcripts are also expected to be subject to nonsense-mediated decay. Arg107 itself is a surface residue (relative accessibility 0.59, 14.7 A from Ap5A) that is not conserved in chicken or mouse AK1, so the nonsense change acts through truncation and not through loss of that side chain. Lys155ArgfsTer39 is different: the new stop falls at codon 193, one codon before the native stop, so the transcript should escape decay and encode a full-length protein whose last forty residues, including the C-terminal helix and the ATP-site residue Gly177, are replaced by unrelated sequence. Siblings homozygous for Arg107Ter had undetectable erythrocyte activity.

nodes.description: Mice lacking Ak1 are viable. Published studies describe skeletal muscle and heart: the enzyme defect is reproduced and energetic economy is reduced under load, with compensation by glycolytic, guanylate kinase and creatine kinase phosphotransfer. Red-cell survival, hematology and neurodevelopment are not described in the papers cited here, so the model informs the enzyme-level defect and the capacity for compensation, not the hemolytic phenotype.

nodes.description: The mature erythrocyte has no mitochondria and cannot synthesize purines de novo, so its adenine nucleotide pool depends on glycolytic ATP production, adenine salvage, and adenylate kinase to return AMP to ADP. In enzyme-deficient red cells the transfer of phosphate between ATP and ADP continues at a small fraction of the normal rate (about 1/2,000 of normal activity in one study), and labeled adenine still enters ADP and ATP at about half the expected rate. The residual flux has been attributed to trace AK2, to guanylate kinase accepting AMP, or to an AMP:GTP phosphotransferase. Steady-state ATP is normal or raised in most patients studied, which reflects the young red-cell population, so a simple fall in ATP does not explain the hemolysis; reported abnormalities are instead raised 2,3-diphosphoglycerate and, in one patient, reduced AMP.

nodes.description: AK1 is the major cytosolic adenylate kinase. It catalyzes the reversible, magnesium-dependent transfer of the terminal phosphate of ATP to AMP (AMP + ATP = 2 ADP), which is the only route by which a cell returns AMP to the ADP and ATP pool without degrading it, and it sets the AMP signal that reports cellular energy state. In affected individuals erythrocyte adenylate kinase activity is undetectable or reduced to between roughly a fifth and a half of normal, and heterozygous parents have about half-normal activity. Erythrocyte activity is the feature the disease is defined by. Other cell types keep part of their adenylate kinase activity through the genetically independent isozyme AK2, which is not thought to be present in erythrocytes in more than trace amounts.

nodes.description: Arg97 is one of the AMP-site residues 94-97 of the CORE domain; its side chain is 3.5 A from the AMP adenine in PDB 1Z83 (2.9 A in 2C95) and it contacts Leu66, Gln101 and Tyr153. It is invariant in vertebrate AK1 and in E. coli and yeast adenylate kinase. The recombinant enzyme loses about 89% of catalytic efficiency with weaker binding of ATP, AMP and ADP. A published tabulation lists the allele in a Japanese child with severe anemia and psychomotor delay (PMID:40016400); the likely primary report, a Japanese letter on splenectomy in this disease (PMID:28211224), has no abstract and could not be checked as its source. It is the most frequent published disease allele in gnomAD (40 alleles, no homozygotes).

nodes.description: Gln101 is an AMP-site residue: its side-chain amide is 3.1 A from N1 of the AMP adenine in PDB 1Z83 and it is buried (relative accessibility 0.04). It is conserved in vertebrate AK1 and in E. coli and yeast adenylate kinase. Lysine cannot make the paired hydrogen bonds that read the adenine base and introduces a charge in the pocket. Not tested as a recombinant enzyme; the homozygous patient had about 12% of normal erythrocyte activity.

nodes.description: The first allele identified. Arg128 lies on a CORE-domain helix (residues 122-133); its guanidinium group is 3.4 A from Ap5A in PDB 1Z83 and it contacts Gly18 and Ser19 of the phosphate-binding loop. It is invariant in vertebrate AK1 and in E. coli and yeast adenylate kinase. Tryptophan removes a phosphate-binding positive charge and adds bulk beside the P-loop; the recombinant human enzyme has about one ten-thousandth of wild-type catalytic efficiency and the chicken equivalent is also less soluble.

nodes.description: Removes one of two adjacent aspartates at the end of the LID domain. Asp140 and Asp141 are both buried (relative accessibility 0.08 and 0.05) and form the salt-bridge network that positions Arg132, Arg138 and Arg149 on the phosphates; Asp140 is 4.0 A from Ap5A. Losing one residue shifts the register of the LID return strand and breaks that network. Recombinant catalytic efficiency is about one ten-thousandth of wild-type.

nodes.description: Late frameshift whose new stop is at codon 193, one codon before the native stop. The homozygous proband also carried alpha- and beta-thalassemia trait and had about 60% of the reference enzyme level by an immunoassay, so the contribution of this allele to his severe anemia is uncertain.

Cysteine leaves a cavity in the hydrophobic core. The recombinant enzyme is grossly perturbed in stability, unlike the catalytic-site alleles tested beside it, and the homozygous patient had no detectable enzyme.

nodes.description: Reported in a child with severe hemolytic anemia (PMID:37782390, a letter with no abstract to quote). The protein change given here was computed from the published nucleotide change on NM_000476.3 and has not been checked against the letter's own wording. Val173 is on a CORE beta-strand (residues 170-174), fully buried (relative accessibility 0.00), 9.9 A from Ap5A, and packs against Tyr117, Val118 and His189; the position is hydrophobic in every ortholog examined. Glycine would leave a cavity in the sheet, so a stability defect is the expected mechanism. Not tested as a recombinant enzyme.

Gln24 is the first residue after the phosphate-binding loop (ATP-site residues 18-23), buried (relative accessibility 0.04), 5.2 A from an Ap5A phosphate and packed against Val179, Val182, Phe183 and Val186 of the C-terminal helix. It is conserved in vertebrate AK1 and in E. coli and yeast adenylate kinase. A buried charge here would disturb the packing that holds the P-loop against the C-terminal helix. Not tested as a recombinant enzyme. Found in trans with Arg138His.

nodes.description: A proposed consequence of AK1 loss in the brain, where AK1 is among the most highly expressed adenylate kinases: reduced adenylate kinase phosphotransfer and AMP signaling in neurons during development. The supporting observation is only that neurological features cluster in patients with absent or very low erythrocyte activity (homozygous Arg107Ter, Arg97Trp, and compound heterozygotes carrying Arg138His); patients with equally absent activity and normal development are also on record, and severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia is a competing explanation that the case reports do not exclude.

evidence.reference_title: Severe erythrocyte adenylate kinase deficiency due to homozygous A-->G substitution at codon 164 of human AK1 gene associated with chronic haemolytic anaemia.
evidence.snippet: No AK band was detected in the AK electrophoresis of the proband, in whom the erythrocyte 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3DPG) and glutathione (GSH) concentrations were normal whereas adenosine triphosphate (ATP) concentration, pyruvate kinase (PK) and glucose-6P-dehydrogenase (G6PD) activities were increased, reflecting the high reticulocyte count (6.9%).

nodes.description: Removal of the spleen for severe or transfusion-dependent hemolysis. It produced complete remission of hemolysis in five patients of one kindred; experience is limited to case reports and no controlled data exist.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital haemolytic anaemia associated with adenylate kinase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Splenectomy performed in five of the six patients resulted in complete remission of the haemolytic process.

nodes.description: Enlargement of the spleen, often with hepatomegaly, from sustained clearance of red cells.

evidence.reference_title: Red cell adenylate kinase deficiency: molecular study of 3 new mutations (118G>A, 190G>A, and GAC deletion) associated with hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
evidence.snippet: One of these patients, a boy of Spanish origin, exhibited a neonatal icterus and splenomegaly and required blood transfusions until the age of 2 years.

evidence.reference_title: Rare hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by a novel homozygous mutation, c.301C > A, (Q101K), in the AK1 gene in an Indian family.
evidence.snippet: He had a hepatosplenomegaly with a liver 4 cm in size and spleen up to the umbilicus.
